review_notes: I read the whole file and searched Mathlib's AlgebraicGeometry directory for existing gluing or sup-of-partial-maps APIs. I found none: RationalMap.lean has no PartialMap.glue, so `glueHom` and `glue` are new API, and `glue` is a named specialisation of `glueHom`. The only overlap I found is the open cover of a union. The file builds a two-element `Cover.mkOfCovers Bool` cover of `p.domain ⊔ V` by hand, twice, instead of using Mathlib's `Scheme.Opens.iSupOpenCover` over `Bool`. Uncertainty: `iSupOpenCover` covers `⨆ b, U b`, not `U ⊔ V`, so a replacement needs a one-line `isoOfEq` or `copy` bridge, or a small shared binary-cover helper. I did not test either option. I treat this as a modest finding.

findings.excerpt:
Cover.mkOfCovers Bool
        (fun b ↦ match b with
          | false => V.toScheme
          | true => p.domain.toScheme)
findings.problem: The file builds the same two-element open cover of `U ⊔ V` by `U` and `V` twice, once in `glueHom` and once in `hom_ext_sup` (lines 140-160). Each copy carries its own surjectivity proof and openness instances. It is a hand-rolled version of Mathlib's `Scheme.Opens.iSupOpenCover`, which is the standard cover of a union of opens by its members. Nothing in the file's docs or uses says why a separate Bool-indexed construction is needed. Because it is built inline, the cover has no name, and the proofs have to unfold it with `change`, `extract_lets` and `dsimp (config := { zeta := false }) only [glueHom]`.
findings.proposed_change: Define one cover of the union, either as a private def used by both `glueHom` and `hom_ext_sup`, or as `Scheme.Opens.iSupOpenCover` over `Bool` (`fun b => cond b U V`) transported along the equality `⨆ b, cond b U V = U ⊔ V` (for example with `X.isoOfEq`). Then `glueHom`'s `hom` is `C.glueMorphisms k _`, and `hom_ext_sup` is `C.hom_ext`. The second hand-built cover and its surjectivity and instance proofs go away.
findings.benefit: Removes about 20 duplicated lines. The cover is built once, or reuses Mathlib's lemmas about `iSupOpenCover`, so `ι_glueMorphisms` and `hom_ext` can be applied without re-unfolding a local `let`. A reader sees that the construction is the standard cover of a union rather than a one-off object.

evidence.excerpt:
let C : (U ⊔ V).toScheme.OpenCover :=
    Cover.mkOfCovers Bool
      (fun b ↦ match b with
        | false => V.toScheme
        | true => U.toScheme)
